title: Trade-history/ledger table + realized-loss-aware 6% Rule
description: The book's actual 6% Rule formula has two parts: realized losses for the current month PLUS risk on currently open trades. `total_open_risk_pct` (backend/app/portfolio/risk.py) only ever implements the second part -- there is no trade-history/ledger model in the schema at all (app/db/models.py has PositionORM/AccountORM/WatchlistItemORM/OHLCVCacheORM, nothing recording a closed position's realized P&L or close date). Concretely: a user who took three straight stopped-out losses earlier this month, then opens a new, individually-fine 2%-sized position, sails right past the 6% Rule today. Add a closed-trade table (ticker, entry/exit price+date, quantity, realized P&L, and an exit-reason tag per Elder's own taxonomy -- target hit / stop hit / reached value zone / going nowhere / starting to turn / couldn't stand the pain / recognized junk trade after entry), populate it when a position closes, and extend the 6% Rule computation to sum this-month's realized losses alongside open-position risk. This table is also the prerequisite for backend-trade-grading and the trade journal frontend task -- design its schema with those in mind even though implementing them is out of scope here.

checklist.step: Design and add the closed-trade ORM table (ticker, quantity, entry/exit price+date, realized P&L, exit-reason tag) to backend/app/db/models.py, with a migration.
Hook position-close (find/confirm the existing delete-position code path in backend/app/api/routers/portfolio.py) to record a closed-trade row instead of just deleting state.

Extend the 6% Rule computation (a new function alongside total_open_risk_pct, or an extension of it -- decide and record) to sum this calendar month's realized losses from the new table plus existing open-position risk.
Unit tests covering: a month with prior realized losses that pushes a new, individually-fine position over the 6% threshold; a fresh calendar month correctly excluding the prior month's losses.
Regenerate backend/openapi.json/frontend types if any response shape changed; document in docs/Analyse.md §7.

decisions.decision: exit_reason is a Python StrEnum (app.portfolio.models.ExitReason) with Elder's 7 taxonomy tags (target_hit, stop_hit, reached_value_zone, going_nowhere, starting_to_turn, couldnt_stand_the_pain, recognized_junk_trade_after_entry) plus an 8th app-only value, 'unspecified', used as the default. Stored on ClosedTradeORM as a plain String column (no DB-level enum/CHECK constraint), mirroring OHLCVCacheORM.interval's existing 'plain string, Python-layer validation only' convention -- SQLite has no native enum type to enforce it at the DB layer regardless.
decisions.rationale: Elder's own taxonomy has no catch-all category, but DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} has no reliable way to infer why the user is closing a position (no target-price/stop-order concept is tracked anywhere in this app), so an explicit-but-optional query param with a non-Elder default was needed. Rejected: making exit_reason required on DELETE (would break/complicate the existing delete UX for a field the frontend doesn't collect yet -- that's the trade-journal task's job); inferring a reason algorithmically from price-vs-stop/price-vs-channel (would require fetching/recomputing protective_stop and the Autoenvelope band inside what's otherwise a simple DB delete, adding a data-provider dependency risk to an endpoint that must keep working even when a position's price/history can't be fetched).

decisions.decision: DELETE /api/portfolio/positions/{id} prices the closed_trades row's exit_price from today's latest close via the same market-data lookup GET /api/portfolio and GET /api/portfolio/risk already use for current_price (app.portfolio.pricing.latest_close, promoted from a private _latest_close to a public function since it now has two callers) -- not a caller-supplied exit_price. If that fetch fails (unknown/delisted ticker, provider unavailable), the position is still deleted, but no closed_trades row is recorded.
decisions.rationale: This app already treats 'current market price' as the authoritative mark-to-market source everywhere else (never a client-supplied number), so pricing the exit the same way is consistent rather than introducing a second, inconsistent pricing path. A data-provider outage must never block removing a position (deleting is the one operation that should always succeed, since a stuck position blocks nothing else the user might want to do), and a closed trade with no real exit price would poison realized_pnl (and so the 6% Rule) with a fabricated number -- silently skipping the closed_trades row is preferable to inventing a price or failing the whole DELETE.

decisions.decision: The 6% Rule's realized-losses-this-month component is a new sibling function, app.portfolio.risk.realized_losses_pct(account, realized_losses_this_month), not a single combined function alongside/replacing total_open_risk_pct. The calendar-month closed_trades DB query itself lives in a new router-level helper, app.api.routers.portfolio._realized_losses_this_month_pct, which sums both via simple addition at the GET /api/portfolio/risk call site. The RiskResponse field keeps its existing name total_open_risk_pct for the combined total (its description is updated to explain both halves), plus a new realized_losses_this_month_pct field exposing the realized-losses half on its own for transparency/debuggability.
decisions.rationale: app.portfolio.risk has no DB dependency anywhere else (Account/Position are plain domain models, not ORM rows) -- a single combined function would have to either take an already-summed dollar figure (making it barely different from two sibling functions summed by the caller) or import SQLAlchemy/ClosedTradeORM itself (breaking that module boundary for one caller). Keeping total_open_risk_pct's own behavior/tests untouched (it still means exactly what its existing unit tests already assert) avoids rewriting a well-covered, already-shipped function's contract. Renaming the RiskResponse field instead of keeping total_open_risk_pct was considered and rejected: it is the field this response has always compared against the 6% threshold and existing frontend code (RiskPanel.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.tsx) already reads it under this name -- broadening its documented meaning costs less than a rename that would ripple through the frontend for no behavioral gain.

decisions.decision: Closing a position via DELETE does not adjust AccountORM.cash (no automatic credit of sale proceeds back to the cash balance).
decisions.rationale: Matches the existing, already-shipped precedent: POST /api/portfolio/positions (buying/adding a position) likewise never debits cash. Cash is entirely user-managed (docs/Analyse.md §9: 'cash balance entered or imported by the user'), and introducing automatic cash bookkeeping on the sell side only, while the buy side stays manual, would be an inconsistent half-measure -- a full auto-cash-sync feature (if ever wanted) belongs in its own task covering both sides.

decisions.decision: Did not update the frontend's 'Total Open Risk' StatCard label/copy (RiskPanel.tsx, RiskSummaryCard.tsx) to reflect that the underlying field now also includes this month's realized losses, beyond the minimal fixture changes needed to keep tsc/tests passing against the widened RiskResponse type.
decisions.rationale: This task is scoped backend/db (skill add-api-endpoint, no add-frontend-feature); a genuine label/copy change would ripple across both risk components, their unit tests, PortfolioPage.test.tsx, DashboardPage.test.tsx, two Storybook stories, and two Playwright e2e specs -- real UI-facing feature work, not a type-compatibility fix, and better scoped to the already-planned frontend-trade-journal task (or its own follow-up) where the realized-losses breakdown can be surfaced properly (e.g. showing the two components separately) rather than a quick label edit here.
